title: From Rome to Alexandria
intro: A traveller leaves Rome for Alexandria. Roads, coastal hops and open-sea crossings each have their own speed and cost: sea transport cost roughly one twenty-eighth of road transport per kilometre (Diocletian's Price Edict, 301 CE). From November to March the open sea was 'closed' (mare clausum) and ships kept to the coasts. Pick the month and the speed of the ships, and see which route is fastest, how long it takes and how far it is compared with the straight geodesic distance.
